---
title: "Fit sampled zeros in Northern cod survey data"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tinyAM)
guide_root <- Sys.getenv("TINYAM_GUIDE_ROOT")
source_files <- if (nzchar(guide_root)) {
  c(list.files(file.path(guide_root, "R"), "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE),
    file.path(guide_root, "NAMESPACE"))
} else {
  list.files(system.file("R", package = "tinyAM"), full.names = TRUE)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  cache.extra = list(R = getRversion(), RTMB = packageVersion("RTMB"),
    sources = unname(tools::md5sum(source_files)), inputs = cod_obs))
```

The Northern cod autumn survey recorded zero at several ages during the years
of low abundance. Those observations can help distinguish a small catchable
cohort from one the survey would usually detect. This example uses the
NCAM-inspired model from the [comparison guide](compare-assessments.html) to
ask how the survey observation family affects the estimated stock history.

## Identify sampled zeros

Set up the survey at the modeled age resolution before choosing a family.
In a local copy of `cod_obs`, sum the index across ages 14–20 where all ages
have an observation. An all-missing survey year stays missing. Keep the
weights and maturity through age 20 so tinyAM can calculate biomass within
the plus group.

```{r inputs}
dat <- cod_obs
rv <- dat$index
older <- rv$age >= 14
groups <- split(rv[older, ], rv$year[older])
pooled <- vapply(groups, function(d) {
  if (identical(sort(as.integer(d$age)), 14:20)) sum(d$obs) else NA_real_
}, numeric(1))
rv$obs[rv$age == 14] <- pooled[as.character(rv$year[rv$age == 14])]
dat$index <- rv[rv$age <= 14, ]

s <- subset(dat$index, year %in% 1983:2025 & age %in% 2:14)
s$status <- factor(ifelse(is.na(s$obs), "Missing",
  ifelse(s$obs == 0, "Zero", "Positive")),
  levels = c("Positive", "Zero", "Missing"))
table(s$status)
```

```{r sampled-ages, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.4, fig.cap="Survey observations by year and age. Orange cells are recorded zeros. Grey cells are missing surveys. Age 14 includes sampled fish ages 14 and older."}
vals <- c(Positive = "#006d81", Zero = "#f05c28", Missing = "#dddddd")
plot(s$year, s$age, pch = 15, col = vals[s$status],
  xlab = "Year", ylab = "Age", yaxp = c(2, 14, 6))
legend("topleft", legend = names(vals), col = vals, pch = 15,
  horiz = TRUE, bty = "n")
```

## Compare observation families

Fit the NCAM-inspired structure with lognormal observations, then change the
family of the Fall 2J3KL survey. The Poisson-link delta lognormal uses the
survey prediction to determine both the chance of zero and the size of
positive observations. Its prediction represents the mean over zeros and
positives. In the lognormal fit, the prediction represents the conditional
median. See the [observation family equations](../reference/observation_families.html).

```{r fits, cache=TRUE, results="hide"}
ncam <- fit_tam(dat, years = 1983:2025, ages = 2:14,
  N_settings = list(process = "off", init = "exp"),
  rec_settings = list(process = "rw"),
  F_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_form = ~ 1, mean_ages = 5:14),
  M_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_supplied = ~ I(0.3),
    age_breaks = c(2, 5, 8, 14), mean_ages = 5:14),
  catch_settings = list(sd_form = ~ 1),
  index_settings = list(sd_form = ~ 1, q_form = ~ mono(q_block)),
  silent = TRUE
)

ncam_pld <- update(ncam, index_settings = list(
  family = list("Fall 2J3KL" = pld_lognormal())
))
```

```{r checks}
check_tam(Lognormal = ncam, PLD = ncam_pld)
subset(tidy_par(ncam_pld)$fixed, par == "y50_index",
  select = c(survey, est, lwr, upr, unit))
```

`y50_index` is the predicted survey index with an even chance of a sampled
zero. The interval comes from the fitted model. Check how well the model
predicts zeros at each age, since agreement in the overall count can hide
age or year patterns.

```{r calibration, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.4, fig.cap="Observed and fitted zero frequency by survey age. Each pair uses the same observed years. Age 14 is the plus group."}
d <- subset(tidy_obs_pred(ncam_pld)$index, is_observed)
d$zero <- as.numeric(d$obs == 0)
cal <- aggregate(cbind(zero, p_zero) ~ age, d, mean)
plot(cal$age, cal$zero, pch = 16, ylim = c(0, 1),
  xlab = "Age", ylab = "Zero frequency")
lines(cal$age, cal$p_zero, lwd = 2, col = "#006d81")
legend("topleft", c("Observed", "Fitted"), pch = c(16, NA),
  lty = c(NA, 1), col = c("black", "#006d81"), bty = "n")
```

```{r residuals, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.4, fig.cap="Quantile residuals for the PLD survey fit. Orange marks sampled zeros, with a reproducible random position in their fitted probability interval."}
r <- subset(residuals(ncam_pld, type = "quantile"),
  type == "index" & is.finite(residual))
plot(r$year, r$residual, pch = 16, col = ifelse(r$obs == 0, "#f05c28", "#006d81"),
  xlab = "Year", ylab = "Quantile residual")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
```

Patterns by age or year can reveal shortcomings in the one-scale detection
model. These residuals condition on the fitted population, so they describe
agreement with the data used to fit it.

## See what changes in the assessment

```{r trajectories, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Annual recruitment and spawning biomass from the same NCAM-inspired specification with two observation families. Differences reflect both the inclusion of sampled zeros and the mean interpretation of the PLD prediction."}
recruitment <- get_recruitment(Lognormal = ncam, PLD = ncam_pld)
ssb <- get_ssb(Lognormal = ncam, PLD = ncam_pld)
old <- par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 5, 1, 1))
draw <- function(d, label) {
  plot(range(d$year), range(d$est), type = "n", xlab = "Year", ylab = label)
  lines(est ~ year, d[d$model == "Lognormal", ], lwd = 2)
  lines(est ~ year, d[d$model == "PLD", ], lwd = 2, col = "#006d81")
}
draw(recruitment, "Recruitment (thousand fish)")
legend("topleft", c("Lognormal", "PLD"), lty = 1,
  col = c("black", "#006d81"), bty = "n")
draw(ssb, "Spawning biomass (tonnes)")
par(old)
```

```{r dashboard, eval=FALSE}
vis_tam(Lognormal = ncam, PLD = ncam_pld)
```

This comparison measures sensitivity to the observation assumption. The
[simulation study and report source](https://github.com/PaulRegular/tinyAM/blob/main/analysis/formula_expansion/pld_validation_report.Rmd)
compare fitted and known population histories under controlled observation
models and SimSurvey monitoring.
